key_insight: Imperfect PDE knowledge improves regression convergence rates only below a modeling-error threshold; with exact physics, the studied PDE classes yield rates corresponding to dimension d−1 rather than d.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify when physical constraints can improve learning beyond smoothness alone and identify conditions for near-linear estimator computation.
method: Compare physics-informed regression against a smoothness-only minimax benchmark.
Derive modeling-error thresholds and rates for constant-coefficient elliptic and hyperbolic PDE classes.
Prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors and tune hyperparameters without knowing the modeling error.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence-rate and complexity guarantees, but no empirical datasets or numerical evaluation.
watch_item: The detailed rate guarantees apply to specific PDE classes, and near-linear computation requires additional conditions.
paper_title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
